Russian philosopher Aleksandr Dugin appears on Tucker Carlson's podcast to discuss Klaus Schwab, transgender politics, and AI. Dugin is a political thinker whose books on empire and tradition have drawn wide attention and sharp criticism in the West. Carlson hosts him as a window into Russian thought.

Dugin argues that Western elites, symbolized by Schwab and the Davos circle, push a single model on every nation. He treats fights over gender and AI as parts of one civilizational struggle. Carlson draws him out on what Russia wants instead. The segment preserves a rare long hearing for a thinker many Western readers only meet through hostile summaries.

Author Vince Everett Ellison joins Tucker Carlson to attack what he calls lies sold to Black America. Ellison wrote a book and film with that charge at the center. His style is blunt and preacher-like.

The title names Martin Luther King Jr., hip hop culture, and the Democrats. Ellison argues leaders and stars misled Black voters for gain. He urges a break with the party he blames most. Carlson gives him room to lay out the full case. The episode will stir strong views, which is plainly the guest's intent.
